  MISSION STATEMENT
  The mission of the City of Monterey Park is to provide excellent services
  to enhance the quality of life for our entire community.

  LAND ACKNOWLEDGMENT
  We would like to acknowledge that the land we inhabit today was once known as
  Tovangaar, the home of the Gabrieleño-Tongva people. We show our respect to the
  Gabrieleño-Tongva people, as well as all Indigenous people, past, present, and future,
  and honor their labor as original caretakers of this land. We commit to uplifting the
  Gabrieleño-Tongva people, invite you to acknowledge the history, and join us in caring
  for this land.

GENERAL INFORMATION
Documents related to an Agenda item are available to the public in the City Clerk’s Office located at 320
West Newmark Avenue, Monterey Park, CA 91754, during normal business hours and the City’s website
at http://www.montereypark.ca.gov/AgendaCenter/City-Council-17.

The public may watch the meeting live on the city’s cable channel MPKTV (AT&T U-verse, channel 99
or Charter Communications, channel 182) or by visiting the city’s website at
http://www.montereypark.ca.gov/133/City-Council-Meeting-Videos. Per the Americans with Disabilities
Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please call City Hall at (626) 307-1359
for reasonable accommodation at least 24 hours before a meeting. Council Chambers are wheelchair
accessible.

PUBLIC PARTICIPATION
You may speak up to 5 minutes on Agenda item. You may combine up to 2 minutes of time with another
person’s speaking. No person may speak more than a total of 10 minutes. The Mayor and City Council
may change the amount of time allowed for speakers. Written Communication will be accepted up to 24
hours before the meeting via email to mpclerk@montereypark.ca.gov.

While all comments are welcome, the Brown Act does not allow the City Council to take action on any
item not on the agenda. The Council may briefly respond to comments after Public Communications is
closed. Persons may, in addition to any other matter within the City Council's subject-matter jurisdiction,
comment on Agenda Items at this time. If you provide public comment on a specific Agenda item at this
time, however, you cannot later provide comments at the time the Agenda Item is considered.

TO:  Honorable Mayor and City Council
FROM:  Jessica Serrano, Director of Community Development
SUBJECT:  One-Year Time Extension for Tentative Map No. 73741 (TM-18-01) –
  130-206 South Chandler Avenue, also identified by Assessor’s Parcel
  Numbers 5257-004-019, 5257-004-020, and 5257-004-021.

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Adopting a resolution approving a time extension for Tentative Map No. 73741
  (TM-18-01); and
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

CEQA (California Environmental Quality Act):
The City reviewed the environmental impacts of the extension under the California
Environmental Quality Act (Public Resources Code §§ 21000, et seq. “CEQA”) and the
regulations promulgated thereunder (14 Cal. Code of Regs. §§ 15000, et seq., the “CEQA
Guidelines”). CEQA Guidelines §§ 15060(c)(2), 15061(b)(3), and 15378 exempt activities that
will not result in a direct or reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the
environment, activities where there is possibility that it may have a significant effect on the
environment, and activities that do not constitute a “project” as defined, respectively. This
activity contemplates extending the expiration date of a tentative map and is for general
policies and procedure-making. Accordingly, this activity is exempt from further review.
Additionally, the environmental impacts regarding this request were adequately reviewed in
accordance with the IS/MND adopted by Resolution No. 12135. Consequently, the findings
set forth in Section 3 of Resolution No. 12135 are incorporated by reference as if fully set
forth.
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
Latigo Canyon Development, LLC (“Applicant”) requests a one-year extension for its tentative
map. This application results from a series of actions concerning a 40-unit senior housing
complex at 130-206 South Chandler Avenue. Consideration of this project commenced in
2016 and was most recently considered in 2023. At that time, the City Council extended the
tentative map for the project (TM-18-01) until April 1, 2024. Without additional Council action
to extend TM-18-01, however, the tentative map will expire on August 12, 2024. Other parts
of the overall project, e.g., the conditional use permit, will require noticing and a public hearing
before the City Council at a later date.

Adopting the proposed resolution would extend the expiration date for TM-18-01 until April 1,
2025.

BACKGROUND:
Previous renditions of the underlying project for 130-206 South Chandler Page 3 of
  Avenue  11
  were

considered by the City Council between 2016 and 2020. Decisions regarding these
previous project proposals are reflected in the administrative record (see, e.g., Resolution
No. 11897; PC Resolution No. 04-19; and Council meeting minutes from April 17, 2019,
May 15, 2019, June 5, 2019, December 18, 2019, and February 5, 2020).

On February 5, 2020, the City Council (among other items) adopted Resolution No. 12135
which approved Tentative Map No. 73741 (TM-18-01). This Resolution allows the
Applicant (Latigo Canyon Development, LLC) to subdivide property for the senior housing
project. Ordinarily, this tentative map would have expired February 5, 2020.

The COVID-19 Pandemic interrupted most land use time periods. Because of that
emergency, the City Council adopted Ordinance No. 2219 in 2022 which authorizes the
City Manager to determine how different land use approvals were affected by the
Pandemic. After reviewing Tentative Map No. 73741, the City Manager determined that
the expiration date would be April 1, 2023. Thereafter, in 2023, the City Council approved
a one-year extension of the tentative map until April 1, 2024.

On March 18, 2024, the Community Development Director received a request from the
Applicant to extend the tentative map for another year. A plain reading of the Monterey
Park Municipal Code (“MPMC”) shows that this request was due on March 14, 2024.
Nevertheless, the City accepted the application as timely as of March 19, 2024.

The Applicant, however, failed to pay the fees needed to process the extension request
until June 13, 2024; fees must be paid to allow for processing the map (MPMC §
20.02.060). Under the Subdivision Map Act (Government Code § 66452.6), expiration of
a map is suspended for 60 days or until the City Council renders a decision on the request
– whichever is sooner. Based upon the June 13, 2024 date, TM-18-01 will expire on
August 12, 2024.

Given the City’s interest in promoting these types of residential projects, it seems prudent
for the City Council to consider extending the tentative map’s expiration date. Note that
the map may be extended up to six years total, i.e., until 2026

2024-25 STRATEGIC PLAN GOAL:
Adopting the draft resolution would advance a strategic plan goal to “Strengthen our local
economy and enhance housing opportunities” by enabling the construction of housing
units to add to the City’s housing stock and provide more affordable housing in the City.

FISCAL IMPACT:
No fiscal impacts are anticipated. The Applicant paid for required fees to process this
request.

  A RESOLUTION APPROVING A ONE-YEAR EXTENSION FOR
  TENTATIVE MAP NO. 73741 (TM-18-01) TO SUBDIVIDE PROPERTY
  LOCATED AT 130-206 SOUTH CHANDLER AVENUE

  The City Council of the City of Monterey Park does resolve as follows:

SECTION 1: The City Council finds as follows:

  A.  At the request of the Applicant, Latigo Canyon Development, LLC, the City
  Council approved Tentative Map No. 73741 (TM-18-01) on February 5, 2020
  via Resolution No. 12135. Monterey Park Municipal Code (“MPMC”) §
  20.04.120 provides that tentative maps generally expire 24 months after
  approval unless extended or suspended by operation of law.

  B.  As provided in Ordinance No. 2219 (adopted April 6, 2022), land use
  approvals were suspended during the COVID-19 Pandemic. In accordance
  with Section 6 of Ordinance No. 2219, the City Manager determined that
  TM-18-01’s expiration date was April 1, 2023 (rather than February 5, 2002).

  C.  After the Applicant filed a request for an extension on February 21, 2023, the
  City Council adopted Resolution No. 2023-R40, extending the expiration
  date for TM-18-01 to April 1, 2024.

  D.  While an application for another one-year extension was due on March 14,
  2024, the City nevertheless accepted an application on March 18, 2024
  which was later supplemented on March 19, 2024. That application,
  however, was not perfected until June 13, 2024 when the Applicant paid the
  application fee in accordance with MPMC § 20.02.060 to processing of the
  application.

  E.  Government Code § 66452.6 suspends the expiration of a tentative map for
  60 days or until a final decision is rendered by the City Council. Based upon
  the June 13, 2024 date, TM-18-01 will expire on August 12, 2024.

  F.  The underlying project, i.e., the approved 40-unit senior housing project,
  would provide the City with much-needed housing. Among other things, it
  will help implement the Monterey Park Housing Element which encourages
  development of this type of housing opportunity. Consequently, allowing TM-
  18-01 to expire without additional City Council consideration is not in the
  public interest.

  G.  The City reviewed the Applicant’s request as to environmental impacts under
  the California Environmental Quality Act (Public Resources Code §§ 21000,
  et seq., “CEQA”) and the regulations promulgated thereunder (14 California
  Code of Regulations §§ 15000, et seq., the “CEQA Guidelines”); and

  I.  This Resolution and its findings is based upon the entirety of the
  administrative record including, without limitation, the staff report and
  representations made during the August 12, 2024 special meeting of the City
  Council.

SECTION 2: Environmental Assessment. The City reviewed the environmental impacts of
the extension under the California Environmental Quality Act (Public Resources Code §§
21000, et seq. “CEQA”) and the regulations promulgated thereunder (14 Cal. Code of
Regs. §§ 15000, et seq., the “CEQA Guidelines”). CEQA Guidelines §§ 15060(c)(2),
15061(b)(3), and 15378 exempt activities that will not result in a direct or reasonably
foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment, activities where there is
possibility that it may have a significant effect on the environment, and activities that do
not constitute a “project” as defined, respectively. This activity contemplates extending the
expiration date of a tentative map and is for general policies and procedure-making.
Accordingly, this activity is exempt from further review. Additionally, the environmental
impacts regarding this request were adequately reviewed in accordance with the IS/MND
adopted by Resolution No. 12135. Consequently, the findings set forth in Section 3 of
Resolution No. 12135 are incorporated by reference as if fully set forth.
 .
SECTION 3: Determination. The City Council extends the expiration date for TM-18-01 to
April 1, 2025.

SECTION 4: Reliance on Record. Each and every one of the findings and determinations
in this Resolution are based on the competent and substantial evidence, both oral and
written, contained in the entire record relating to the Project. The findings and
determinations constitute the independent findings and determinations of the City Council
in all respects and are fully and completely supported by substantial evidence in the
record as a whole.

SECTION 5: Summaries of Information. All summaries of information in the findings,
which precede this section, are based on the substantial evidence in the record. The
absence of any particular fact from any such summary is not an indication that a particular
finding is not based in part on that fact.

SECTION 6: Effective Date. This Resolution becomes effective immediately upon
adoption and memorializes the City Council’s final decision made on August 12, 2024.
Note that persons dissatisfied with the City Council’s decision may appeal it in accordance
with applicable law to the Los Angeles Superior Court within 90 days of the City Council’s
decision.

  RESOLUTION NO.

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF MONTEREY
  PARK, CALIFORNIA, DECLARING AND RECOGNIZING THE MONTH
  OF AUGUST 2024 AS NATIONAL BACK-TO-SCHOOL MONTH

  BE IT RESOLVED by the Council of the City of Monterey Park as follows:

SECTION 1: The City Council finds as follows:

  A. August marks the beginning of a new academic year for millions of students across
  the United States and has been recognized as National Back-to-School Month
  since the 1960s.

  B. National Back-to-School Month is a time for families and caregivers across the
  nation to prepare their children for the upcoming school year and ensure they are
  equipped with the necessary supplies, knowledge, and mindset to start the school
  year successfully.

  C. National Back-to-School Month highlights the importance of a smooth transition
  from summer break to the classroom and encourages families, caregivers, and
  students to set new routines and focus on everyone’s safety and mental well-being.

  D. It is important that families and caregivers prioritize their children’s mental health
  to ensure a seamless transition back to school. Families and caregivers are
  encouraged to establish school-day routines early (e.g., homework and bedtime),
  encourage open communication, and incorporate positive reinforcement.

  E. Public schools in the City of Monterey Park are served by the Alhambra, Garvey,
  Los Angeles, and Montebello school districts. Monterey Park is also home to
  numerous private schools as well as East Los Angeles College.

  F. The Monterey Park Bruggemeyer Library provides excellent resources to ensure
  students, parents, caregivers, and teachers have a successful school year.
  Available resources include online tutoring, databases, e-books, and websites.
  More information can be found on the Monterey Park Bruggemeyer Library’s
  website at https://www.montereypark.ca.gov/282/Children.

  G. The Monterey Park City Council encourages all students to have a successful
  school year by taking on new challenges, making meaningful connections with
  their peers, and sharpening their skills to become even better learners and hereby
  proclaims August 2024 as National Back-to-School Month.

SECTION 2: Electronic Signatures. This Resolution may be executed with electronic
signatures in accordance with Government Code §16.5. Such electronic signatures will
be treated in all respects as having the same effect as an original signature.
